# WoW Loot Systems: DKP, EPGP, Loot Council, and What Actually Works

Every WoW guild eventually fights about loot. This is the working comparison of DKP, EPGP, Loot Council, and Wishlist systems - what each actually rewards, what each silently punishes, and how to pick the one your roster won't quit over.

edit\_note By Jade Finch calendar\_today May 3, 2026 history Updated June 7, 2026

rocket\_launch Leading WoW players? [Build your guild site free →](https://guildorder.com/register?utm_source=guides&utm_medium=article&utm_campaign=loot-systems-dkp-vs-epgp)

There is no neutral loot system.
Every system rewards a behavior, punishes another behavior, and has a drama vector hiding in week ten of progression. The guilds that survive a full tier without a loot blowup didn't pick the "fair" system; they picked the one their roster's culture was honest enough to support. This guide is the working comparison of the four systems modern guilds actually run, what each one is biased toward, and how to choose without rebuilding the matrix mid-tier. WoW Classic guilds run a different set - soft-reserve, GDKP, and 40-man DKP - covered in the WoW Classic loot-systems guide .

lightbulb

Who this is for

Officers picking or replacing a loot system. Raid leaders who keep getting dragged into loot disputes. Trial members trying to understand why their guild does loot the way it does. Applies to Heroic and Mythic raiding; LFR uses Personal Loot and rarely needs an officer-managed system.

## The four systems people actually run

Modern WoW guilds run one of four systems.
Anything else is a variant of one of these four wearing a different name.

DKP
    Earn points for raid attendance and boss kills. Spend points on items via blind or open bid.

EPGP
    Earn 'Effort Points' for showing up. Accumulate 'Gear Points' when you take loot. Priority is the EP/GP ratio. Self-balancing.

Loot Council
    Officers decide who gets each item. No formula. Speed and discretion at the cost of perceived fairness.

Wishlist (TMB / RCLootCouncil with imports)
    Each raider pre-ranks every item in the tier. Drops are awarded by wishlist priority, often with a tiebreaker.

Group Loot is the default system for Normal, Heroic, and Mythic raids - all three difficulties use it. (Loot system choice interacts heavily with how the raid leadership team manages disputes - a permissive raid lead can run Loot Council, a hands-off one cannot.) Casual Normal guilds can let Group Loot roll unmanaged without much drama.

...

The drama vector is **GP cost decisions** . Officers set GP costs per slot and per item type. If two-handers cost 600 GP and trinkets cost 400 GP, raiders will start optimizing what they bid on. The system is only as fair as the GP table, and the GP table is set by humans.

### Loot Council is fast and opaque

Loot Council is what every loot system devolves into when the formula breaks down. An item drops, three officers in a private channel decide who gets it, and the answer is announced. No bid, no formula, no waiting room.

Loot Council rewards **roster optimization** . Officers can give the tier set piece to the raider whose performance jumps most from it, the trinket to the player whose sim says it's a 4% upgrade rather than the player whose sim says 1.5%, and the off-hand weapon to the alt that's about to be brought into Mythic next reset. The same loot allocated by EPGP would land on whoever's `EP / GP` was highest, which is often not the right answer.
The drama vector is **the council itself** . Every loot decision is a judgment by named humans. If those humans are also the friends-of-the-leader who get loot decisions in their favor, the guild dies of perceived nepotism by week eight. Loot Council requires a council whose composition is visibly broader than the friend group, and a written rubric that the council can refer back to when challenged.

warning

The council failure mode

Loot Council guilds blow up not because the wrong raider got the loot, but because the council never wrote down its criteria. When a raider asks "why didn't I get that?", the answer needs to point at a written rubric, not at "we discussed it." If you can't produce the rubric, you don't have Loot Council; you have favoritism with extra steps.

### Wishlist systems reward planning

Wishlist systems (TMB, RCLootCouncil with imported wishlists, wowaudit-driven priorities) take the runtime decision out of loot entirely.

...

The systems below all carry administrative overhead that is not worth it for Heroic or below. If yes, continue.
2. ### Does your roster trust your officer team?
   
   If your raiders trust the officer team's judgment, Loot Council is faster, more flexible, and produces better roster outcomes per item. If your raiders don't trust the officers - or if your officers haven't earned the trust yet because the guild is new - skip Loot Council. It will collapse.
3. ### Are your raiders willing to sim and wishlist every reset?
   
   If yes, a Wishlist system is the most analytically optimal allocation you can run, and it requires the least mid-pull officer attention. If your raiders can't be bothered to sim, Wishlist degrades into "I forgot to update my list, why didn't I get the trinket?" Don't run it.
4. ### Do you have raiders joining mid-tier?
   
   DKP punishes mid-tier joiners brutally unless you implement a starting-point or decay system. EPGP self-corrects within 3-4 weeks.
Loot Council and Wishlist treat new raiders fairly by default.
5. ### What's your average raid roster turnover?
   
   High turnover guilds (>30% per tier) should run EPGP or Wishlist; the system has to absorb new raiders without manual rebalancing. Low-turnover guilds can run DKP or Loot Council without churn pain.

## Addon and tooling reality

Every system above has at least one mature addon. The administrative overhead is in officer training, not the addon.

DKP
    Core Loot Manager (CLM) is the current default in 2025-2026 Classic raiding and supports DKP, EPGP, and roll modes from a single config. MonolithDKP and CommunityDKP still work but most active guilds have migrated off them.

EPGP
    EPGP Lootmaster (classic) or RCLootCouncil with EPGP module (retail). Wowaudit can drive automatic decay and import.

Loot Council
    RCLootCouncil. Universal. Add the wowaudit integration for sim data, alts, and historical context inline at award time.

Wishlist

...

## Cross-cutting truth

Loot is the second-most-common reason raiders leave guilds. The first is officer drama. Loot is the secondary because every loot dispute is also an officer-drama dispute wearing a different costume.

The guilds that survive long-term don't have the perfect system; they have an honest system that the roster believes the officers will administer consistently. Pick the one whose drama vector you can manage, write the rules down, run it for a full tier without changes, and then evaluate. That's the whole craft.

excerpts:
The systems we will cover include GDKP, DKP, Loot Council, Master Loot, Soft Reserve, MS>OS, and Personal Loot. It is important to note that different versions of the game utilize completely different frameworks. What is standard practice in WoW Retail might be mechanically impossible or heavily restricted in Classic. Similarly, community-driven formats that thrive in Classic environments operate under strict developer guidelines on newer, specialized realms like TBC Anniversary.

## GDKP (Gold Dragon Kill Points) — How It Works

[Gold](https://frostyboost.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/Gold-1024x452.webp)

When asking what is gdkp world of warcraft players are often referring to one of the most discussed loot formats in the game. GDKP WoW runs replace random rolling or arbitrary points with the game’s universal currency: gold.

The mechanics are highly structured. When a boss is killed and an item drops, the raid leader links the item in the chat and opens an in-raid auction.

...

* **Not for PUGs:** The system is completely incompatible with pickup groups since points hold no value outside the specific guild.
* **Roster Dependent:** It falls apart if the guild lacks a stable, consistent group of recurring players.

## Loot Council — How It Works

[Loot Council](https://frostyboost.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/Loot-Council.webp)

A loot council wow setup completely removes currency, points, and random rolls from the equation. Instead, a designated group of guild officers forms a council to decide exactly who receives each dropped item.

The council bases their decisions on multiple factors to optimize the raid’s overall power. They consider which class benefits most mathematically from the item’s stats, a player’s recent attendance, their performance, and how big of an upgrade the item is compared to what the player is currently wearing. The ultimate goal is to equip the raid to defeat harder bosses, rather than simply rewarding individual players.
### Loot Council Pros

* **Optimizes Raid Progression:** Gear is funneled to the exact classes and players who will provide the most benefit to the entire group.
* **High Flexibility:** The council can easily adapt to unexpected drops or unique situations.
* **No Currency Required:** Players do not need to farm gold or hoard points to get gear.

### Loot Council Cons

* **Highly Subjective:** Decisions rely on human judgment, which can lead to favoritism.
* **Drama Potential:** Players who are passed over for gear often feel slighted, leading to arguments and tension.
* **Requires Deep Trust:** The entire system collapses if the guild members do not fully trust their officers.
* **Unusable for PUGs:** Strangers will never trust an arbitrary council of organizers to distribute loot fairly.

## Master Loot — How It Works

[Master Loot](https://frostyboost.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/Master-Loot.webp)
To understand master loot wow mechanics, you have to look at the baseline tool provided by the game client itself. When Master Loot is enabled, the raid leader gains complete manual control over every item on a boss’s corpse. Players cannot loot the boss directly; the raid leader selects the item and assigns it directly into a specific player’s inventory.

Historically, this was the primary tool used to facilitate systems like DKP and Loot Council in Classic versions of the game. In modern Retail, the developers have heavily restricted or entirely removed this feature for unorganized groups to prevent abuse.

### Master Loot Pros

* **Rapid Distribution:** A decisive raid leader can hand out items instantly, keeping the raid moving fast.
* **Total Control:** Mistakes are eliminated because only one person handles the gear.
* **Transactional Efficiency:** It is highly convenient for organized guild runs or structured events.

### Master Loot Cons

...

Trading these items to other players is generally restricted unless the item is a lower or equal item level to what you already possess in that slot.

### Personal Loot Pros

* **Mathematically Fair:** Each player receives their own individual loot roll without competing against other raid members.
* **Zero Drama:** Because the game makes the decision, players cannot argue with the raid leader or accuse officers of favoritism.
* **Zero Administration:** The system requires no organizers, no spreadsheets, and no websites.

### Personal Loot Cons

* **No Agency:** You have absolutely no control over what items you receive.
* **Wasted Drops:** You may receive duplicate items that you cannot trade away due to system restrictions.
* **Poor for Progression:** Guilds cannot funnel powerful trinkets or tier sets to their best players to help clear difficult content.

link Link

Loot distribution is one of the most important - and most contentious - systems in World of Warcraft guild life. How your guild handles loot affects morale, retention, and whether your best players stick around or /gquit after losing a BiS item to someone who joined last week.

This guide covers every major loot system used by WoW guilds, how each works, and which fits your guild best.

...

Loot Council (LC) puts gear decisions in the hands of the guild's officers. When an item drops, officers discuss who would benefit most and assign it accordingly.

Factors typically considered:

* **Upgrade size** \- Is this a 30 ilvl upgrade or a 5 ilvl sidegrade?
* **Attendance and commitment** \- Does this player show up reliably?
* **Role importance** \- Would this upgrade benefit the raid more on a tank than a DPS?
* **Recent loot** \- Has this player received a lot of gear recently?

### RCLootCouncil

The dominant addon for managing loot council is **RCLootCouncil** , with over 32 million downloads. It streamlines the voting process - when loot drops, raiders indicate their interest (BiS, minor upgrade, transmog), officers discuss and vote, and the addon records everything.

### Pros

* **Optimal distribution** \- Officers can consider context that point systems can't (like gearing the main tank before a progression boss)
* **Flexible** \- No rigid formulas.
Decisions adapt to the guild's current needs.
* **Used by almost all Cutting Edge guilds** \- The standard at the highest level of play

### Cons

* **Trust required** \- Players must trust that officers are fair. Perceived favoritism is the number one source of loot drama.
* **Transparency concerns** \- "Why did the officer's friend get the trinket?" kills guilds
* **Officer burden** \- Making loot decisions is stressful, especially on contested items

### Making Loot Council Work

The key phrase every guild leader cites: **"What matters most is that your entire guild believes in the system."** Publish your loot priorities, explain decisions when asked, and maintain a public log of every distribution.

## Suicide Kings [[edit]]( "Edit section")

A simpler alternative: all raiders sit on a priority list. When you take an item, you drop to the bottom of the list ("suicide"). The person at the top always has first choice.

* **Pros:** Dead simple, no math, no officer judgment
* **Cons:** Inflexible, no way to prioritize upgrades by value, encourages passing on minor upgrades to preserve position

## Which System Fits Your Guild? [[edit]]( "Edit section")

|Guild Type |Recommended System |Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
|Casual / social guild |Group Loot (default) |No overhead, everyone rolls, drama is rare at this level |
|Regular raiding (Normal/Heroic) |EPGP |Self-balancing, fair, moderate complexity |
|Progression guild (Heroic/Mythic) |Loot Council |Optimal distribution for progression, requires trust |
|Classic WoW guild |DKP or EPGP |Classic tradition, addons like Core Loot Manager support both |
|Pickup group / PUG raid |Group Loot (default) |No trust established, let the game handle it |

## The Shift From Personal Loot [[edit]]( "Edit section")

WoW used **Personal Loot** as the default (and eventually mandatory) system from Warlords of Draenor through Shadowlands.
